scenes.title: The Disk I/O Bottleneck
scenes.text: In database engines, reading a disk block is a hundred thousand times slower than system memory. If an index requires dozens of random seeks per query, throughput collapses.

scenes.title: Binary Tree vs B-Tree Fan-out
scenes.text: A binary tree stores one key per node. For a billion rows, searching down thirty levels demands thirty disk round-trips. But a B-Tree packs hundreds of keys per node, crushing tree depth to three levels.

scenes.title: Page Alignment & Traversal
scenes.text: Each B-Tree node matches a physical storage block, like an eight-kilobyte page. Fetching one page loads dozens of sorted keys into memory at once, routing queries to the target leaf in single hops.

scenes.title: Balanced Growth: Node Split
scenes.text: When insertions fill a page to capacity, it splits and promotes the median key upward. The tree grows from the bottom up, guaranteeing balanced logarithmic access across billions of records.
